findings.detail: Child SA cb80b636 shows the length signature of an 8-byte block cipher, so DES or 3DES, at 60% confidence.
findings.remediation: Replace the 64-bit block cipher (DES or 3DES) with AES-GCM-256, or AES-CBC-256 with HMAC-SHA2-256.
findings.standard: RFC 8221 section 5: ENCR_3DES is SHOULD NOT, ENCR_DES is MUST NOT
findings.threat: Birthday-bound collision attack against the ESP payload
findings.title: A 64-bit block cipher is in use on ESP

findings.remediation: Replace 3DES with AES. Its 64-bit block makes collisions practical once a single key has protected a few hundred gigabytes.
findings.standard: RFC 8247 section 2.1 lists ENCR_3DES as SHOULD NOT; RFC 8221 the same for ESP
findings.threat: Birthday-bound collision attack against a 64-bit block cipher
findings.title: 3DES encryption negotiated for the IKE SA

findings.detail: Key exchange used group 2 (MODP_1024), about 80 bits of security.
findings.remediation: Move to group 19, 31 or 14. The small fixed MODP groups are shared across so many deployments that one precomputation effort attacks all of them.
findings.standard: RFC 8247 section 2.4 lists groups 2, 5, 23 and 24 as SHOULD NOT
findings.threat: Precomputation attack against a widely shared small modulus
findings.title: A weak key exchange group was negotiated

findings.detail: The responder selected ENCR_3DES/AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96/PRF_HMAC_SHA1/DH2 at about 80 bits, while ENCR_AES_CBC-256/AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128/PRF_HMAC_SHA2_256/DH14 at about 112 bits was offered.
findings.remediation: Align the two policies so the strongest suite both ends support is the one selected, and remove the weaker options from both proposal lists.
findings.standard: NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 guidance on configuring the strongest mutually supported suite
findings.threat: Downgrade, whether by policy mismatch or by an active attacker
findings.title: The responder selected a weaker proposal than the strongest offered

findings.detail: The IKE SA integ is AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96.
findings.remediation: Move to HMAC-SHA2-256. SHA-1 is not yet broken for HMAC use, so this is a planning item rather than an emergency.
findings.standard: RFC 8247 sections 2.2 and 2.3 rate SHA-1 as MUST-, meaning it is expected to be downgraded
findings.threat: Weakening integrity protection as collision attacks improve
findings.title: SHA-1 used as the IKE integrity algorithm or PRF

findings.detail: The IKE SA prf is PRF_HMAC_SHA1.
findings.remediation: Move to HMAC-SHA2-256. SHA-1 is not yet broken for HMAC use, so this is a planning item rather than an emergency.
findings.standard: RFC 8247 sections 2.2 and 2.3 rate SHA-1 as MUST-, meaning it is expected to be downgraded
findings.threat: Weakening integrity protection as collision attacks improve
findings.title: SHA-1 used as the IKE integrity algorithm or PRF

findings.detail: 1 of 2 offered proposals are below 112 bits: ENCR_3DES/AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96/PRF_HMAC_SHA1/DH2 (~80 bits).
findings.remediation: Remove the weak proposals from the initiator configuration. Offering them means any responder that prefers them will be accommodated.
findings.standard: NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 guidance on restricting proposals to acceptable suites
findings.threat: Downgrade surface that an active attacker can steer toward
findings.title: Weak proposals were offered alongside strong ones

findings.detail: No SPI change was seen across 1 child SA(s) in 4s of capture, so no rekey interval could be measured.
findings.remediation: This is usually a short capture rather than a long lifetime. Capture for longer than the configured lifetime before treating it as a real finding.
findings.standard: NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 on limiting SA lifetime
findings.threat: Extended exposure of a single key, and more data protected under it
findings.title: No SA rekey was observed within the capture

findings.detail: No RFC 8784 post-quantum pre-shared key and no RFC 9370 additional key exchange was signalled, and the negotiated group is classical.
findings.remediation: For traffic that must stay confidential for a decade or more, consider RFC 8784 post-quantum pre-shared keys or an RFC 9370 hybrid key exchange. Informational: few deployments are expected to have this today.
findings.standard: RFC 8784 (post-quantum pre-shared keys), RFC 9370 (multiple key exchanges)
findings.threat: Record now, decrypt later, once a quantum computer becomes available
findings.title: No post-quantum protection was signalled

warnings: The responder rejected 1 initial IKE_SA_INIT attempt(s) (INVALID_KE_PAYLOAD) before agreeing. A rejected key exchange group means the group finally used was the responder choice rather than the initiator preference, which is worth checking against policy.
